findings.title: The documented `rule_refused` remedy still says "share the agent", unlike the changed admin message.
findings.body: The addendum to the CSO report says the two sentences an admin reads after a refused re-address no longer say "share the agent". They now tell the admin to make sure the agent is shared with the person and that the person can sign in. This table row still lists "share the agent with its primary contact or with the people in the role" as the remedy. That points admins away from the blocked or deactivated cause this PR adds. The fix is to reword this row to match the new message.

findings.title: The troubleshooting remedy for a held credential entry leaves out the blocked and deactivated causes.
findings.body: This change makes blocked and deactivated accounts unable to open the agent. Elsewhere in the PR, the remedy for `role_cannot_open_agent` was reworded to "make sure the agent is shared with them and that they can sign in". This line still says the entry waits only until an admin shares the agent or assigns a primary contact. Suppose the primary contact is blocked from the Workspace. An admin who follows this line finds the agent already shared, and the entry stays held. The fix is to use the same wording as approvals.md: the entry waits until an admin makes sure the agent is shared with its primary contact and that they can sign in, or assigns one.

held.title: Public `reachable_people` was removed without a replacement under that name.
held.body: The change deletes `role_addressing.reachable_people`, and its two callers in this file now use the new `reach_of`. If any module outside this diff still calls `role_addressing.reachable_people`, for example a delivery or answer fence in `ask_service` or client_portal, that call now raises `AttributeError` when it runs, and the ask or decision path fails. I could not see the rest of the repo to confirm there are no such callers. Either check with a grep, or keep a thin wrapper: `def reachable_people(agent_name, people): reach = reach_of(agent_name, people); return [p for p in people if reach[p]]`.
